summary: The draft is well cited on adaptive data analysis and post-selection inference, but the IRT-based reporter, the ML model-selection optimism claim in the introduction, and the prompt-optimizer family lack direct citations.
missing_literatures: item response theory / latent-difficulty models (psychometrics and LLM evaluation)
selection bias and overfitting in ML model selection and hyperparameter search

rewrite_targets.reason: The EB-IRT reporter is named for item response theory and uses a logistic latent-ability/difficulty model with hierarchical priors and Laplace-based empirical-Bayes fitting, yet no IRT, Rasch or hierarchical-IRT reference is cited. Reviewers will expect the model lineage to be credited and related to existing IRT-based LLM evaluation.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: each logged outcome follows y_{qk} ~ Bernoulli(sigma(a_k - b_q))
search_topics: Rasch model / item response theory foundations
hierarchical Bayesian item response models with empirical-Bayes or Laplace fitting
item response theory for language model benchmark evaluation

rewrite_targets.reason: The core claim that the best-of-search score is a biased, over-optimistic estimate and that the usual interval ignores selection is stated without support from the ML model-selection and hyperparameter-search literature, where this is a well-known problem. Related work covers only statistical and holdout-reuse literature plus one image-classification study, so positioning against ML selection bias is thin.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: It is therefore a biased estimate of that candidate's accuracy on new questions, and the usual interval around it ignores the selection.
search_topics: over-fitting in model selection and selection bias in performance evaluation
bias in cross-validation error estimates when selecting among many models
meta-analysis of benchmark overfitting from repeated test-set reuse

rewrite_targets.reason: The paragraph on prompt search names only DSPy, MIPRO and a best-arm formulation as the optimizers whose reported scores are at risk. Well-known LLM-driven prompt optimizers are not cited, so the claim that none of these works supplies a post-search score with selection-aware uncertainty rests on a narrow sample.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: DSPy and MIPRO automate prompt and pipeline optimization
search_topics: automatic prompt optimization with large language models
evaluation overfitting in prompt optimization on small validation sets
